patients.label: 21-year-old primigravida woman with ALCAPA syndrome diagnosed by echocardiography during pregnancy

identity_evidence.quote: we present the case of a 21-year-old woman diagnosed with ALCAPA syndrome during pregnancy

attribution_limitations: The discussion says a prompt cardiac examination, potentially including Holter monitoring, should have been performed. It does not state that Holter monitoring was or was not done, and no Holter fact is recorded.

The text says the weekly monitoring covered the whole gestation but gives no dates for the echocardiography, ECG or start of medical therapy relative to the 15-week presentation, so their order relative to each other is not stated beyond the recorded relations.

Pixel text printed in the ECG image header includes a sex word and in the CT image a date and device-reported fields; these pixel values do not match or extend the text and are kept only in visual.json.

The syncope was initially attributed to maternal stress, and the discussion calls the resulting delayed diagnosis a critical oversight, but the source never explicitly refutes stress as a factor. Maternal stress is kept as a provisional initial attribution.
Hospitalization at 38 weeks was for preeclampsia evaluation; the result of that evaluation, the indication for the emergency cesarean and the gestational age at delivery are not stated.

evidence.quote:
Figure 1.
The image shows the first ECG of the patient.

Figure 2.
The 2D echocardiography, in the parasternal long-axis view, shows a dilated right coronary artery, which is a sign of anomalous left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA) in echocardiography.

Figure 3.
The 2D echocardiography with color flow mapping, in the parasternal short-axis view, demonstrates abnormal flow within the left coronary artery toward the main pulmonary artery.

Figure 4.
The parasternal short-axis view on 2D echocardiography with color flow mapping demonstrates coronary collateral vessels supplying myocardial perfusion.

Figure 5.
The postpartum computed tomography angiography demonstrates an anomalous origin of the left main coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA), confirming the diagnosis of ALCAPA syndrome.

claims.text: A 21-year-old primigravida woman presented at 15 weeks of gestation with atypical chest pain and severe weakness, with heart rate 98 bpm and blood pressure 110/65 mm Hg. She reported shortness of breath and fatigue since childhood without an identified cause, and an episode of hypotension and syncope in the eighth week of pregnancy that was initially attributed to maternal stress. Her only medications were folic acid and prenatal vitamins.
